content.content:
# Unattended follow-up to a scheduled reindex + recall eval (Task Scheduler, \Eric\memsearch-drain-*).
# Runs as the last action of the task, after memsearch-drain.ps1 and recall-eval.py:
#   1. checks the index finished (memsearch-drain.log ends in exit=0),
#   2. checks recall-eval wrote ledger rows in the last 24 h,
#   3. commits + pushes the ledger and results in ~/.claude (nothing else on Windows does),
#   4. writes LATEST.md here with the rows,
#   5. ONLY on a problem, appends one line to .errors.log, which every session surfaces
#      at startup (same pattern as claude-stack-doctor/weekly-check.ps1).
param([string]$Label = '', [switch]$Test)   # -Test: no git, no .errors.log

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$claude = Join-Path $HOME '.claude'
$errLog = Join-Path $claude 'global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log'
$problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

$drainLog = Join-Path $claude 'scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$drainLast = if (Test-Path $drainLog) { Get-Content $drainLog -Tail 1 } else { '' }
$indexOk = $drainLast -match 'exit=0'
if (-not $indexOk) { $problems.Add("index did not finish cleanly (last drain line: '$drainLast')") }

$ledger = Join-Path $here 'ledger.md'
$since = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$rows = @()
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $rows = @(Get-Content $ledger | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\| (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) ' -and $Matches[1] -ge $since -and (-not $Label -or $_ -match [regex]::Escape("| $Label"))})
}
if ($rows.Count -eq 0) {
    $last = Join-Path $here "logs\last-$Label.txt"   # written by run-eval.ps1
    $why = if (Test-Path $last) { " [$((Get-Content -LiteralPath $last -Raw).Trim())]" } else { '' }
    $problems.Add("recall-eval wrote no ledger rows$(if ($Label) { " labelled '$Label'" }) in the last 24 h$why")
}

$git = 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe'
$pushed = $false
if ($rows.Count -gt 0 -and -not $Test) {
    & $git -C $claude add -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
    & $git -C $claude diff --cached --quiet -- audits/recall-eval
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        & $git -C $claude commit -q -m "recall-eval: scheduled run $(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd) $Label" -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude pull -q --no-rebase --no-edit 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude push -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
        $pushed = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
        if (-not $pushed) { $problems.Add('commit made but git push failed (run git pull/push in ~/.claude)') }
    } else { $pushed = $true }
}

$status = if ($problems.Count) { 'PROBLEM: ' + ($problems -join '; ') } else { 'OK' }
@(
    "# Latest scheduled recall eval"
    ""
    "Run finished $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') on $env:COMPUTERNAME. Status: $status"
    "Index: $drainLast"
    ""
    "| date | machine | label | backend | n | hit@1 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 ms | p95 ms | fail% | coverage% | by layer (hit@5) |"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
) + $rows | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'LATEST.md') -Encoding utf8

if ($problems.Count -and -not $Test) {
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $errLog -Encoding utf8 -Value "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] recall-eval scheduled run: $($problems -join '; ') - see ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/LATEST.md"
}
exit 0
=== drain head
# memsearch-drain.ps1 -- one-off foreground catch-up of the memsearch backlog.
#
# Why (2026-09-28, Windows laptop): ~10,100 chunks were never indexed. The
# SessionEnd hook caps each run at 600s and this CPU embeds ~5 s/chunk with
# bge-m3, so every run was killed after ~110 chunks and the next session end
# restarted it -- 2.5-3 GB of RAM all day. This runs the same incremental
# index with no cap, once, then gets out of the way.
#
# Coordination: holds ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.lock
# with THIS process's PID for the whole run (the hook skips while the owner is
# alive), and refreshes .memsearch-last-run so the hook's 30-min cooldown is in
# force when it finishes. Runs BelowNormal so interactive work keeps the CPU.

# Runs as the last action of the task, after memsearch-drain.ps1 and recall-eval.py:
#   1. checks the index finished (memsearch-drain.log ends in exit=0),
#   2. checks recall-eval wrote ledger rows in the last 24 h,
#   3. commits + pushes the ledger and results in ~/.claude (nothing else on Windows does),
#   4. writes LATEST.md here with the rows,
#   5. ONLY on a problem, appends one line to .errors.log, which every session surfaces
#      at startup (same pattern as claude-stack-doctor/weekly-check.ps1).

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$claude = Join-Path $HOME '.claude'
$errLog = Join-Path $claude 'global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log'
$problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

$drainLog = Join-Path $claude 'scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$drainLast = if (Test-Path $drainLog) { Get-Content $drainLog -Tail 1 } else { '' }
$indexOk = $drainLast -match 'exit=0'
if (-not $indexOk) { $problems.Add("index did not finish cleanly (last drain line: '$drainLast')") }

$ledger = Join-Path $here 'ledger.md'
$since = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$rows = @()
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $rows = @(Get-Content $ledger | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\| (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) ' -and $Matches[1] -ge $since -and (-not $Label -or $_ -match [regex]::Escape("| $Label"))})
}
if ($rows.Count -eq 0) {
    $last = Join-Path $here "logs\last-$Label.txt"   # written by run-eval.ps1
    $why = if (Test-Path $last) { " [$((Get-Content -LiteralPath $last -Raw).Trim())]" } else { '' }
    $problems.Add("recall-eval wrote no ledger rows$(if ($Label) { " labelled '$Label'" }) in the last 24 h$why")
}

$git = 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe'
$pushed = $false
if ($rows.Count -gt 0 -and -not $Test) {
    & $git -C $claude add -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
    & $git -C $claude diff --cached --quiet -- audits/recall-eval

        & $git -C $claude push -q 2>&1 | Out-Null

        if (-not $pushed) { $problems.Add('commit made but git push failed (run git pull/push in ~/.claude)') }
    } else { $pushed = $true }
}

    "# Latest scheduled recall eval"
    ""
    "Run finished $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') on $env:COMPUTERNAME. Status: $status"
    "Index: $drainLast"
    ""
    "| date | machine | label | backend | n | hit@1 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 ms | p95 ms | fail% | coverage% | by layer (hit@5) |"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"

# The one action of \Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly: drain -> recall eval -> after-run.
# Replaces the task's three separate actions (2026-10-04). On 10-01 and 10-04 the second
# action died at 02:10 with 0xC0000142 (STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED): the process never got far
# enough to run a line, whether it was python.exe or pwsh. It runs fine by hand and in a
# probe task while logged in, so it is a start-up failure in the overnight session, not the
# script. Running the steps from here lets a step that fails to start be retried.
param([string]$Label = 'weekly', [string]$Backends = 'memsearch,fts5,rg,jev')

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$pwsh = 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe'
$log = Join-Path $here 'logs\weekly-chain.log'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $log) | Out-Null
function Log([string]$s) { Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Encoding utf8 -Value "[$(Get-Date -Format s)] $s" }

$DLL_INIT_FAILED = -1073741502   # 0xC0000142 as a signed exit code

function Step([string]$name, [string[]]$argv) {
    for ($try = 1; $try -le 4; $try++) {
        & $pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File @argv
        $code = $LASTEXITCODE
        Log "$name try=$try exit=$code"
        if ($code -ne $DLL_INIT_FAILED) { return $code }
        [Threading.Thread]::Sleep(30000)
    }
    return $code
}

Log "start label=$Label"
Step 'drain' @((Join-Path $HOME '.claude\scripts\memsearch-drain.ps1')) | Out-Null
Step 'eval' @((Join-Path $here 'run-eval.ps1'), '-Label', $Label, '-Backends', $Backends) | Out-Null
# after-run checks the drain log and the ledger itself, so it always runs.
Step 'after-run' @((Join-Path $here 'after-run.ps1'), '-Label', $Label) | Out-Null
Log 'end'

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

name: automation-cadence
description: "Standing automation schedule on Mac + Windows — ritual nudges, memsearch reindex + recall eval timing, OS audit cadence, gws/Gmail capability limits, reMarkable OCR entry point"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 330c1f71-242a-47c7-ac7b-129bd6f5dd3c
  modified: 2026-10-03T23:04:15.787Z
---

Durable schedule and capability facts for the Mac automation stack. These are stable
settings, not active threads — health-check them with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Ritual nudges — OFF on both machines (updated 2026-10-03)

- Mac `com.keystone.rituals` was booted out and disabled **2026-09-24**; Windows
  `KeystoneOS-Rituals` (weekdays 17:00, Fri 15:30) is disabled and Eric chose to **keep it
  off** on 2026-10-03. Nothing nudges `/interview-me` or `/weekly-review` any more.
- The reminder now is `~/DEV/WORKFLOW.md` (the ideal day/week) plus the status lines.
  `ritual-check.ps1` still works by hand. It has **five** rituals (interview-me,
  weekly-review, harvest, forecast-capture, `slate` added 09-14); `Name    = ` in
  `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` is the authoritative list. Due/overdue is computed
  from each ritual's own output (forecast-capture is Monday-anchored and season-bounded —
  see [[cfb-forecast-capture]]).

**The output artifact is the record**, not a reminder firing.

## memsearch reindex

**Mac:** reindex **rides the daily backup task** rather than running on its own timer
(00:30 → 09:00 on 2026-08-29 → **21:00 since 2026-09-24**, per claude-stack-doctor). The
backup's uncapped full reindex absorbs backlogs the short SessionEnd hook can't finish.
See [[backup-sync-system]].

**Windows:** no nightly reindex — the `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` task is disabled (since
2026-08-13). Task Scheduler `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` (**Sundays 02:00**) chains
`memsearch-drain.ps1` → `audits/recall-eval/recall-eval.py` (memsearch, fts5, rg, jev;
label `weekly`) → `audits/recall-eval/after-run.ps1`, which commits+pushes the results,
writes `LATEST.md`, and appends to `.errors.log` only on a problem. `\Eric\memsearch-drain-once`
is the same chain for one-off runs (last armed 2026-09-30 22:30, label `post-vault-index`).

## OS audits

Full OS audit last run **2026-07-24** (reports under `audits/`, guards auto-run);
**next due 2026-10-24**.

## Capability limits worth remembering

- **gws `invalid_client: The provided client secret is invalid` = stale client SECRET, not
  token rot** — re-auth alone never fixes it. The secret for client `208643585660-3ogm…`
  (project `baylor-gws`) was rotated 2026-09-17 to one ending `Xyjf`; the Mac kept the
  June one until 2026-09-30, when the Windows copy was carried over via Drive. Console no
  longer shows or downloads a secret: copy the other machine's `client_secret.json`, or
  Add secret (shown once). Then login, then delete `token_cache.json`.
- **gws** re-auth requires explicit full scope URLs — the `-s drive`
  shorthand silently grants no scopes (v0.22.5 bug), and `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json`
  must be deleted after re-auth or the stale token is served. See [[gws-forms-api]].
- **MCP Gmail is draft-only** — it can compose drafts but must not be treated as a send path.

## reMarkable OCR

`remarkable_extract.py` — USB-first with a `--cloud` fallback; Vision API key lives in
`.env`.

I've fixed the scheduled recall test, but I couldn't reproduce the 2 AM failure, so whether it holds will only show on next Sunday's run.

**Cause.** The weekly task was three separate steps: drain, recall test, then record results. The second step died at 02:10 with code `0xC0000142`, which means the program failed while still starting up and never ran a line of the script. It happened the same way on 10/1 and on 10/4, with different programs in that slot. A test task with the same setup ran fine while I was logged in, so the failure seems tied to the overnight conditions, not the script.

**Fix.** `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` now runs one script, `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/weekly-chain.ps1`, which runs the three steps in order. If a step fails to start with that code, it waits 30 seconds and tries again, up to 4 times. Each step is written to `logs/weekly-chain.log`. The trigger (Sundays 02:00, runs on wake if missed) is unchanged.

**Test.** I ran the new setup through Task Scheduler with a cheap test label. All three steps ran and exited 0, with no retries needed. The fix and the updated automation-schedule memory are committed and pushed in `~/.claude` (`e74afcf`), and I removed the test tasks.

Two side effects:
- The test added a `chain-test` row to the recall ledger, which got pushed.
- It also added a line to `.errors.log`, so you'll see it at the start of your next session.

**A separate problem the test found.** Partway through the drain step, the Milvus container crashed (exit code 1) and restarted itself. That's its 6th restart since it was created, and the logs don't show why. So the drain step in the test ended with exit 1, and `LATEST.md` now reads PROBLEM. Last night's drain at 02:00 was clean. This isn't the start-up failure; it's Milvus itself. Your harness-time budget puts it in the Friday slot, unless it happens again before then.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__create_draft
entries.description:
Creates a new draft email in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool takes recipient addresses (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`), a `subject`, and body content as inputs. Plain text body content can be provided in `body` (do NOT format `body` with Markdown), and rich-text HTML content can be provided in `htmlBody` (use valid HTML tags for formatting; if both are provided, `body` serves as the plain-text alternative). If the draft is created as a reply to an existing message, the ID of the original message should be passed to the tool in the `replyToMessageId` field.

Returns a Draft object with the `id`, `threadId`, and `viewUrl` fields populated.

attachments.description: Optional. The attachments to include in the email. The combined size of attachments in the message cannot exceed 25MB. If you need to send files larger than 25MB, upload the file to Drive first and then insert the Drive link into `body` or `html_body`.

bcc.description: Optional. The blind carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

body.description: Optional. The plain text body content of the email draft. Do NOT format this field with Markdown (such as headers `#`, bold `**`, bullet points `*`, or tables `|`). If formatted rich text is desired, use `html_body` instead. If `html_body` is also provided, this field is treated as the plain-text alternative.

cc.description: Optional. The carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

htmlBody.description: Optional. The HTML content of the email draft. If provided, this will be used as the rich-text version of the email. Use this field (with valid HTML tags such as ` `, `

replyToMessageId.description: Optional. The ID of the message to reply to. If provided, this will be used as the reply-to message ID for the email draft, and the `body` and `html_body` will be appended to the original message body.

subject.description: Optional. The subject line of the email. Defaults to empty if not provided.

to.description: Optional. The primary recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

Attachment.description: Represents an attachment to be included in an email.

content.description: Required. The base64-encoded content of the attachment.

filename.description: Optional. The name of the file to be attached, e.g. "invoice.pdf". For inline attachments, this is used for Content-ID generation. For regular attachments, `filename` is used to specify the filename to email clients. If not provided, the attachment may be received with no name.

id.description: Optional. Output only. When present, contains the ID of an external attachment that can be retrieved in a separate `GetMessageAttachment` request.

inline.description: Optional. If true, this attachment is handled as inline. An inline attachment is a content that is intended to be displayed within the body of an HTML email, as opposed to being listed as a separate file for download. If false or absent, defaults to false, and it's treated as a regular attachment.

mimeType.description: Optional. The field representing a content or media type must use IANA MIME type, https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml. If not provided, defaults to "application/octet-stream".

content.content:
# CATES, Comprehensive Athletic Talent Evaluation System

A data-driven system for evaluating collegiate athletes and recruits, built to support
fit determinations and financial decisions on athlete market value and recruitment
investment. Emphasizes NCAA compliance while giving a competitive advantage through
evidence-based assessment.

## Framework

Four pillars, weighted:

| Pillar | Weight | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Athletic Performance | 35% | Testing metrics, force plate, GPS, speed, technical skills |
| Academic Profile | 25% | GPA, course load, academic progression and motivation |
| Psychological Assessment | 25% | Mental performance (S2 Cognition and related testing), character |
| Environmental Factors | 15% | Support structure, team and cultural fit |

Medical risk is a prerequisite, assessed separately on an A-F grading scale and layered
over the weighted score. These are the CATES (2025) pillars, canonical since 2026-10-02.

## Stakeholders

Athletic department administrators, financial decision-makers, and supervisors.
They need executive-level materials with clear ROI justification and an
implementation path, not raw analytics.

## Current state

The framework and a full executive presentation package exist, covering financial
projections, implementation strategy, and stakeholder communication. The system
supports two intake speeds: a rapid process for time-limited evaluations (transfer
portal, incoming grad athletes) and a comprehensive process for full comparative
analytics.

## Working notes

- Success measures: recruitment efficiency, reduced injury-related cost, performance outcomes
- Standardized athlete profiles are the unit of comparison
- Transfer portal and incoming graduate athlete evaluation are the highest-value use cases

## Repo layout

- `docs/`: decision records, methodology, framework documentation
- `docs/program/`: the framework documents moved off the cloud project
- `data/`: pointer only. See `data/README.md`.

No source files existed on the primary storage drive when this repo was created.
Content lived in the Claude cloud project only. Add materials here as they are built.

## Related

- S2_Evaluation (cognitive testing that feeds the Psychological Assessment pillar)
- PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026 (athlete profiling)

## Read first

This repo is the source of truth. The Cowork project "Athlete Evaluation Framework" is
only a pointer.

| Read | When |
|---|---|
| `docs/STATUS.md` | Every session, first thing |
| `docs/program/README.md` | To see what moved off the cloud project and what did not |
| `docs/program/comprehensive-athletic-talent-evaluation-system.md` | Current system definition, five weighted components |
| `docs/program/comprehensive-athlete-evaluation-system.md` | Original CAES four-pillar framework, kept for lineage |
| `docs/program/rapid-athletic-cognitive-assessment-protocol.md` | Portal or group evaluation under time pressure |
| `docs/program/executive-white-paper.md` | Stakeholder and ROI conversations |
| `docs/program/baylor-medical-grading-rubric.md` | The A-F medical grade layered over the weighted score |
| `docs/context.md` | Principles and approach carried over from the cloud project |

## Where related code and data live

- `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation`: cognitive testing that feeds the Psychological Assessment pillar
- `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026`: football athlete profiling
- `~/DEV/COG_S2_Position_Reports`: S2 position reporting
- `~/DEV/SportScienceResearchRepo/SourcePapers/`: the total-score-of-athleticism literature
- Deliverables (.docx, .pptx, spreadsheets) go to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` on Google Drive, not this repo
- Athlete-level data goes on the primary storage drive, never in this repo. See `data/README.md`

## Project rules

- Always create new files. Never overwrite an existing one.
- Default to 2025 as the working year in documents unless stated otherwise.
- Credentials come from `.env` on disk. Never pasted into chat, never echoed.
- Third-party platforms stay read-only.
- Baylor design system on every document. Spec in AGENTS.md.
- Financial figures in the white paper are unverified projections. Do not restate them as findings.

## Session routine

Start: `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before anything else.
End: update `docs/STATUS.md`, commit, `git push`.

Durable schedule and capability facts for the Mac automation stack. These are stable
settings, not active threads — health-check them with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Ritual nudges — OFF on both machines (updated 2026-10-03)

- Mac `com.keystone.rituals` was booted out and disabled **2026-09-24**; Windows
  `KeystoneOS-Rituals` (weekdays 17:00, Fri 15:30) is disabled and Eric chose to **keep it
  off** on 2026-10-03. Nothing nudges `/interview-me` or `/weekly-review` any more.
- The reminder now is `~/DEV/WORKFLOW.md` (the ideal day/week) plus the status lines.
  `ritual-check.ps1` still works by hand. It has **five** rituals (interview-me,
  weekly-review, harvest, forecast-capture, `slate` added 09-14); `Name    = ` in
  `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` is the authoritative list. Due/overdue is computed
  from each ritual's own output (forecast-capture is Monday-anchored and season-bounded —
  see [[cfb-forecast-capture]]).

**The output artifact is the record**, not a reminder firing.

## memsearch reindex

**Mac:** reindex **rides the daily backup task** rather than running on its own timer
(00:30 → 09:00 on 2026-08-29 → **21:00 since 2026-09-24**, per claude-stack-doctor). The

"""Daily email: the files Claude created on a given day, grouped by repo, with full paths. "Created by Claude" = added in a git commit whose Co-Authored-By trailer names Claude. Files Claude writes outside git (Drive deliverables, scratch) are not attributable, so they are not listed. Repos are fetched first and read with --all, so the Mac's pushed commits count too. Runs from Task Scheduler (\\Eric\\claude-files-digest, 06:30, reports the previous day). python claude-files-digest.py # yesterday, send python claude-files-digest.py --date 2026-10-03 --dry-run # write HTML, no send """ import argparse import datetime as dt import html import re import subprocess import sys from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor from pathlib import Path HOME = Path.home() DEV = HOME / "Desktop" / "DEV" TO = "Eric_Rash@baylor.edu" NODE = "node" GWS_JS = HOME / r"AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\@googleworkspace\cli\run.js" LOG = HOME / ".claude" / "scripts" / "logs" / "claude-files-digest.log" ERR_LOG = HOME / ".claude" / "global-memory" / "transcripts" / ".errors.log" PER_REPO = 30 # paths listed per repo before "+N more" MAX_BODY = 28000 # Windows command line caps the whole call at 32767 chars # Same health-data filter as project-triage/landed.py, plus session transcripts. SKIP = re.compile( r"(?i)DEXA[_ ]?Project|athlete-snapshots|pff-snapshots|Injur(y|ies)|/Roster/|roster[^/]*\.(xlsx?|csv)$" r"|/Personnel(_Interview_Docs)?/|WBB_athletes|Athlete_Performance_Overview|Spirit Squad|ICE ?Form" r"|^projects/.*\.jsonl$|/tool-results/") def log(msg: str) -> None: LOG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(f"[{dt.datetime.now():%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S}] {msg}\n") def git(repo: Path, *args: str, timeout: int = 60) -> str: r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=timeout) return r.stdout def repos() -> list[Path]: found = [] for parent in (DEV, DEV / "Football", DEV / "SpecialRequests"): if parent.is_dir(): found += [p for p in parent.iterdir() if (p / ".git").exists()] found += [HOME / ".claude", HOME / ".claude" / "skills", HOME / ".claude" / "global-memory", HOME / "Desktop" / "SecondBrain"] return [p for p in found if (p / ".git").exists() and p != DEV] def created(repo: Path, day: dt.date) -> list[str]: try: git(repo, "fetch", "-q", "origin", timeout=45) except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: pass out = git(repo, "log", "--all", f"--since={day} 00:00", f"--until={day + dt.timedelta(days=1)} 00:00", "--diff-filter=A", "--name-only", "--format=%x1e%(trailers:key=Co-Authored-By,valueonly,separator=;)") paths = [] for block in out.split("\x1e")[1:]: lines = block.strip("\n").splitlines() if not lines or "claude" not in lines[0].lower(): continue paths += [p for p in lines[1:] if p.strip() and not SKIP.search(p)] return sorted(set(paths)) def build(day: dt.date, found: dict[Path, list[str]]) -> tuple[str, str]: total = sum(len(v) for v in found.values()) subject = f"Files Claude created: {day:%a %b %d, %Y} ({total} file{'s' * (total != 1)})" parts = [f"

Files added in Claude co-authored commits on {day:%A, %B %d}, across DEV and ~/.claude " f"(both machines, as pushed). {total} files in {len(found)} repos.

"] if not found: parts.append("

Nothing created that day.

") for repo, paths in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])): items = "".join(f"
  • {html.escape(p)}
    • " for p in paths[:PER_REPO]) more = f"
  • +{len(paths) - PER_REPO} more
    • " if len(paths) > PER_REPO else "" block = (f"

    {html.escape(repo.name)} ({len(paths)})

    " f"
    {html.escape(str(repo))}
    " f"
      {items}{more}
    ") if sum(map(len, parts)) + len(block) > MAX_BODY: parts.append(f"

    Truncated to fit one email. Full list: " f"python {html.escape(__file__)} --date {day} --dry-run

    ") break parts.append(block) return subject, "
    " + "".join(parts) + "

Durable schedule and capability facts for the Mac automation stack. These are stable
settings, not active threads — health-check them with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Ritual nudges — OFF on both machines (updated 2026-10-03)

- Mac `com.keystone.rituals` was booted out and disabled **2026-09-24**; Windows
  `KeystoneOS-Rituals` (weekdays 17:00, Fri 15:30) is disabled and Eric chose to **keep it
  off** on 2026-10-03. Nothing nudges `/interview-me` or `/weekly-review` any more.
- The reminder now is `~/DEV/WORKFLOW.md` (the ideal day/week) plus the status lines.
  `ritual-check.ps1` still works by hand. It has **five** rituals (interview-me,
  weekly-review, harvest, forecast-capture, `slate` added 09-14); `Name    = ` in
  `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` is the authoritative list. Due/overdue is computed
  from each ritual's own output (forecast-capture is Monday-anchored and season-bounded —
  see [[cfb-forecast-capture]]).

**The output artifact is the record**, not a reminder firing.

## memsearch reindex

**Mac:** reindex **rides the daily backup task** rather than running on its own timer
(00:30 → 09:00 on 2026-08-29 → **21:00 since 2026-09-24**, per claude-stack-doctor). The
backup's uncapped full reindex absorbs backlogs the short SessionEnd hook can't finish.
See [[backup-sync-system]].

**Windows:** no nightly reindex — the `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` task is disabled (since
2026-08-13). Task Scheduler `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` (**Sundays 02:00**) has ONE
action since 2026-10-04: `audits/recall-eval/weekly-chain.ps1`, which runs
`memsearch-drain.ps1` → `run-eval.ps1` (memsearch, fts5, rg, jev; label `weekly`) →
`after-run.ps1` (commits+pushes results, writes `LATEST.md`, appends to `.errors.log` only on
a problem), retrying a step that exits 0xC0000142. Log: `audits/recall-eval/logs/weekly-chain.log`.
Why: as three separate actions, action 2 died at 02:10 with 0xC0000142 (DLL init failed, never
ran a line) on 10-01 and 10-04; it runs fine by hand. `\Eric\memsearch-drain-once` no longer exists.

**next due 2026-10-24**.

## Capability limits worth remembering

- **gws `invalid_client: The provided client secret is invalid` = stale client SECRET, not
  token rot** — re-auth alone never fixes it. The secret for client `208643585660-3ogm…`
  (project `baylor-gws`) was rotated 2026-09-17 to one ending `Xyjf`; the Mac kept the
  June one until 2026-09-30, when the Windows copy was carried over via Drive. Console no
  longer shows or downloads a secret: copy the other machine's `client_secret.json`, or
  Add secret (shown once). Then login, then delete `token_cache.json`.
- **gws** re-auth requires explicit full scope URLs — the `-s drive`
  shorthand silently grants no scopes (v0.22.5 bug), and `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json`
  must be deleted after re-auth or the stale token is served. See [[gws-forms-api]].
- **MCP Gmail sends to Eric himself are approved** (2026-10-04): `send_message`/`forward` work.
  Eric OK'd sending to eric.rash11@gmail.com and his Outlook, Eric_Rash@Baylor.edu. Anyone
  else still gets a draft, not a send.

content.text:
Starting tomorrow (Monday, 10/5) at 6:30 AM, you'll get a daily email at Eric_Rash@baylor.edu listing the files I created the day before. I sent a test for yesterday (10/3): 554 files. Check your Outlook to confirm it arrived. Gmail accepted it, but I can't see your inbox.

- **What counts as "created":** files added in git commits that carry the Claude co-author line, across every DEV repo, `~/.claude` and the SecondBrain vault. It fetches before reading, so Mac work counts once it's pushed. Files I save outside git, like Drive deliverables, can't be traced to me, so they won't appear. Health-data paths are filtered out, using the same filter as the `landed` ledger.
- **Layout:** grouped by repo. Each group shows the repo's full path, then up to 30 file paths, then "+N more" if there are more.
- **Why the previous day:** a 6:30 AM email covers a whole day, including your Mac evening sessions. If the laptop is asleep at 6:30, the email goes out when it wakes.
- **How it runs:** a local Windows scheduled task, `\Eric\claude-files-digest`, sending through the same `gws` setup as your 5 PM Gmail digest. No cloud scheduler is involved. The script is `~/.claude/scripts/claude-files-digest.py`. Running it with `--date YYYY-MM-DD --dry-run` previews any day without sending. If a send fails, it's logged where your next session start will show it. It's committed and pushed in `~/.claude`.

Most of yesterday's list was Flint (253 files) and vault notes (209). Tell me if you'd rather those two show as a count only, so the email shows the deliverables.

"] if not found: parts.append("

content.text:
Yes for the Mac, and it's small. The phone is harder: the board only runs on whichever laptop started it, so your phone can't reach it.

**Mac app: easy.** The board is already a web page served by `board.py` on your laptop. In Safari (macOS Sonoma or later), open the board and choose File → Add to Dock. That gives it a Dock icon and its own window, like an app.
- One change is needed first: the board picks a random port and access token each time it starts. A Dock app needs a fixed address, so the board would have to use a fixed port and remember its token between starts. That's about a 20-minute change.
- If you want it to start at login, a tiny `.app` wrapper or login item can run `pm`. Same idea, a little more work.

**Phone: the board can't come with you, and I'd keep it that way.** I see three paths:
1. **Use Claude on your phone (recommended).** claude.ai/code can open the `project-triage` repo and run the same `portfolio.py` commands: "log progress on X", "park Y", "what's on my slate". Changes go through git like everything else, so the Mac and Windows boards pick them up at the next sync. Nothing new to build.
2. **Make the laptop board reachable from your phone** over Wi-Fi or a VPN like Tailscale. The laptop has to be awake, it opens a port on a Baylor-managed machine, and Tailscale is a cloud service. Your rule needs Baylor IT approval for that. I'd skip it.
3. **A hosted mobile board** (a claude.ai artifact with its own database). It works anywhere, but it becomes a second copy of the registry. That's the stale-view problem the PM design retired on 10/3, when the frozen artifact was replaced. I'd skip it too.

So my suggestion is the Safari Dock app for the Mac and Claude on your phone, with nothing new built for mobile. The fixed-port change is system work, so by your harness-time budget it belongs in Friday's slot (10/9).

Should I log it for Friday, or make the fixed-port change now?

    path.write_text(json.dumps({"pid": os.getpid(), "port": port, "token": token,
                                "repo": str(Path(repo).resolve())}), encoding="utf-8")


def running_instance(repo: Path, path: Path | None = None) -> str | None:
    """URL of a live board for this repo, or None. Live = it answers its own token."""
    path = path or state_path()
    try:
        st = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if Path(st["repo"]) != Path(repo).resolve():
            return None
        base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{int(st['port'])}"
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}/api/changes?token={st['token']}&names=", timeout=2) as r:
            if r.status != 200:
                return None
        return f"{base}/?token={st['token']}"
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        return None


def start_background(args) -> int:
    """Start the board as a child of this terminal (it dies with it), wait until it answers."""
    log = state_path().with_suffix(".log")
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), "--repo", str(args.repo),
           "--port", str(args.port), "--no-open"]
    if args.dev_root:
        cmd += ["--dev-root", str(args.dev_root)]
    with open(log, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
        subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    for _ in range(60):
        url = running_instance(args.repo)
        if url:
            print(f"board started at {url}")
            if not args.no_open:
                webbrowser.open(url)
            return 0
        time.sleep(0.25)
    print(f"board did not start; see {log}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Local portfolio board")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).parent)
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--no-open", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dev-root", type=Path, default=None,
                    help="default: the folder holding project-triage")
    ap.add_argument("--background", action="store_true",
                    help="what `pm` and /pm run: reuse a running board, else start one and return")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    portfolio.load_registry(args.repo / "portfolio.json")   # refuse to start on a bad file

    url = running_instance(args.repo)
    if url:
        print(f"board already running at {url}")
        if not args.no_open:
            webbrowser.open(url)
        return 0
    if args.background:
        return start_background(args)

    backup = session_backup(args.repo)
    if backup is not None:
        print(f"session backup: {backup}")

    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    srv = make_server(args.repo, token, args.port, args.dev_root)
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}/?token={token}"
    state = state_path()
    write_state(state, args.repo, srv.server_address[1], token)
    print(f"board at {url}")
    print("ctrl-c to stop")
    if not args.no_open:
        webbrowser.open(url)
    try:
        srv.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nstopped")
    finally:
        try:                                  # only clear the state if it is still ours
            if json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("pid") == os.getpid():
                state.unlink()
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            pass
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

class TestSingleInstance(unittest.TestCase):
    """`pm` / `/pm`: start the board if it isn't running, else reuse the one that is."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dir = Path(self.tmp.name)
        seed(self.dir)
        self.state = self.dir / "state.json"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def test_no_state_file_means_not_running(self):
        self.assertIsNone(board.running_instance(self.dir, self.state))

    def test_a_live_server_named_in_the_state_file_is_found(self):
        srv = board.make_server(self.dir, "tok", port=0)
        threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        try:
            board.write_state(self.state, self.dir, srv.server_address[1], "tok")
            url = board.running_instance(self.dir, self.state)
            self.assertEqual(url, f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}/?token=tok")
        finally:
            srv.shutdown(); srv.server_close()

    def test_a_dead_server_or_another_repo_is_not_reused(self):
        srv = board.make_server(self.dir, "tok", port=0)
        port = srv.server_address[1]
        srv.server_close()                                      # nothing listening now
        board.write_state(self.state, self.dir, port, "tok")
        self.assertIsNone(board.running_instance(self.dir, self.state))
        board.write_state(self.state, self.dir / "elsewhere", port, "tok")
        self.assertIsNone(board.running_instance(self.dir, self.state))

    def test_background_starts_once_and_then_reuses(self):
        import os, subprocess, sys
        for f in ("board.py", "board_ops.py", "portfolio.py", "cards.py", "landed.py", "seven_day.py",
                  "sweep.py"):
            shutil.copy(REPO / f, self.dir / f)
        env = {**os.environ, "PM_BOARD_STATE": str(self.state)}
        cmd = [sys.executable, str(self.dir / "board.py"), "--background", "--no-open", "--repo", str(self.dir)]
        first = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=60)
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0, first.stderr)
        pid = json.loads(self.state.read_text())["pid"]
        try:
            url = first.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1].split()[-1]
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r:
                self.assertEqual(r.status, 200)
            again = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=60)
            self.assertIn(url, again.stdout)
            self.assertIn("already running", again.stdout)
            self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.state.read_text())["pid"], pid)
        finally:
            try:
                os.kill(pid, 9)
            except OSError:
                pass

    """Decision 10: the header says how many registry edits have not reached GitHub."""

    def git(self, cwd, *a):
        import subprocess
        subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True)

    def test_not_a_repo_is_none(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            self.assertIsNone(board.unpushed_edits(Path(t)))

    def test_counts_a_dirty_registry_and_unpushed_registry_commits(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            root = Path(t)
            origin, work = root / "origin.git", root / "work"
            self.git(root, "init", "-q", "--bare", str(origin))
            self.git(root, "clone", "-q", str(origin), str(work))
            for k, v in (("user.email", "t@t"), ("user.name", "t"), ("commit.gpgsign", "false")):
                self.git(work, "config", k, v)
            reg = work / "portfolio.json"
            reg.write_text("{}\n")
            self.git(work, "add", "."); self.git(work, "commit", "-qm", "seed")
            self.git(work, "push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD")
            self.git(work, "branch", "-q", "--set-upstream-to", "origin/" + self._branch(work))
            self.assertEqual(board.unpushed_edits(work), 0)
            reg.write_text('{"a": 1}\n')
            self.git(work, "commit", "-qam", "data: board edits")
            (work / "other.txt").write_text("x")
            self.git(work, "add", "."); self.git(work, "commit", "-qm", "not the registry")
            self.assertEqual(board.unpushed_edits(work), 1)
            reg.write_text('{"a": 2}\n')
            self.assertEqual(board.unpushed_edits(work), 2)

    def _branch(self, work):
        import subprocess
        return subprocess.run(["git", "branch", "--show-current"], cwd=work, capture_output=True,
                              text=True).stdout.strip()

        self.assertIn("visibilitychange", page)

# project-triage — the project board

**New to the board? Start with [`docs/GUIDE.md`](docs/GUIDE.md)**: the daily and weekly
loop, how to read a card, and a 30-minute hands-on walkthrough.

The one list of Eric's projects (`portfolio.json`, the **registry**) and the live
board that is its front door. Built to prevent one failure: losing the thread on a
project already known about. Design: `docs/project-management-system-design.md`
(decided 2026-10-03; built the same day, stages 1–9).

```
  terminal (portfolio.py, /project) ─┐                 ┌─ each repo's docs/STATUS.md
  board page (drag, Start/Park/Done) ─┼─→ portfolio.json ─┤
  closeout / weekly-review rituals ───┘                 └─ landed ledger (both machines)
                                            │
                                    board.py (127.0.0.1) ── polls every 3 s, re-renders
```

Tasks stay in each repo's `docs/STATUS.md`; the board reads them and never owns
them. The page edits registry fields only. The static `render.py` → `dashboard.html`
(and its published Artifact and `pulse.md`) retired on 2026-10-03.

## Starting the board

```
pm                      # PowerShell profile / ~/.zshrc function
/pm                     # in Claude Code (mod in ~/.claude/mods/pm)
python board.py --background
```

All three reuse the board already running on this machine (pid/port file in the temp
dir), or start one tied to the terminal and open it; it stops when that terminal
closes. `dev-sync` starts it after a clean `git pull` of this repo. `python board.py`
alone runs it in the foreground (Ctrl-C stops it).

The URL carries a per-run token; `/api/*` refuses requests without it, writes must be
same-origin, and it binds 127.0.0.1 only.

## What the board shows

- **Resume cards.** Each project: what it is (`purpose`), where it stands (newest
  dated STATUS entry), next step (first STATUS `## Next` item, else `next_action`),
  last touched (landed ledger, either machine), who it is for (receiver), the 7-day
  countdown while a start is unproven, and flags for a missing next step or receiver.
- **Focus view** (default): active rows, paused rows touched in the last 14 days, and
  rows with a charter date in the next 14 days. **All rows** turns it off; **search**
  covers every lane and badges the lane tabs. Columns say how many rows the view hides.
- **Live.** Terminal edits to the registry, or to a shown project's STATUS.md, appear
  within ~3 s. A change that lands while you type or drag waits until you finish.
- **Header nudges:** paused rows awaiting the Friday sweep; unpushed registry edits.

## What the board changes

- Columns are stages; tabs are lanes (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`).
  Dragging sets the stage, the drop position sets priority (`rank` is recomputed).
- **Start / Park / Done** in the open card, the status pill, and the terminal's
  `portfolio.py set-status` all go through one function: a Start over the slate cap
  (`meta.slate.cap`, job lane) is refused with the reason, and a Start begins the
  7-day clock.
- Purpose, next action, receiver (a name, or `me: <why>`), notes, lane.
- Inbox: drag onto a stage to promote (lands active), onto Archive to retire.
- Undo reverses the last write unless something else wrote the registry since.

Every write validates against `portfolio.validate`, backs up to `portfolio.json.bak`,
and replaces the file atomically (retrying briefly on Windows file locks).

## CLI (`python portfolio.py <verb>`)

| Verb | What |
|---|---|
| `add-idea "<pitch>" --source ..` | capture to the inbox |
| `add-update <name> "<note>" [--next-action ..]` | log progress |
| `set-stage <name> <stage>` | move along the stage ladder |
| `set-status <name> <status> [--note ..]` | start / park / finish (slate cap + 7-day clock) |
| `set-receiver <name> "<who>"` | who the work is for |
| `card-check [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--project X]` | closeout: cards + gaps for projects touched today |
| `sweep` / `sweep-decide <name> revive\|keep\|archive` | the Friday sweep |
| `slate-check`, `seven-day [--apply]`, `week-report`, `mark-done` | slate rules |
| `crosswalk` | drift between the registry, DEV and Drive |

Any registry error prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2, and never touches
`portfolio.json`. `landed.py scan|show` maintains the ledger of where files landed.

## Rituals that keep it true

- **closeout**: `card-check` for every project touched today; fixes gaps (a dated
  STATUS line, a Next item, a receiver) before pushing; commits registry edits alone as
  `data: board edits <date>`; prints the cards last.
- **weekly-review** (Friday): `sweep` puts up to 10 paused rows untouched 30+ days to a
  decision — revive, keep parked 90 days (`parked_until`), or archive.
- **dev-sync**: pulls this repo, then starts the board.

## Stage ladder

```
idea → grilled → spec → planned → building → shipped
```

Optional per row; rows backfilled on 2026-10-03 sit in an `unstaged` column until
dragged onto a stage.

# Using the project board — a working guide

For Eric. What the README lists, this shows in use. Read top to bottom once
(about 10 minutes), then do **"Your first 30 minutes"** at the end with real projects.

## The idea in four lines

- **The registry** (`portfolio.json`) is the one list of projects. Status, lane, stage,
  receiver, rank live there.
- **Each repo's `docs/STATUS.md`** holds the work itself: what happened (dated lines) and
  what's next. The board reads it and never writes it.
- **The board** is the front door: one card per project, live, editable.
- **Three rituals keep it true**: dev-sync opens it, closeout fixes the cards, the Friday
  review sweeps the paused pile.

The whole system exists so that six weeks from now you can look at a card and pick a
project back up without re-reading the repo.

## Your day with it

**Start.** `dev-sync` (or `/startup`) pulls everything and opens the board. If you skip
that, type `pm` in PowerShell or `/pm` in Claude Code. It reuses the board if one is
already running, so typing it again is harmless.

**During.** Keep the board open beside the terminal. Work happens in the terminal and the
repos; the board catches up within ~3 seconds of any change to the registry or a visible
project's STATUS.md. You don't refresh it. Use the board for the things it is good at:

| You want to… | On the board | Or in the terminal |
|---|---|---|
| See what's live | Focus view (default) | `portfolio.py slate-check` |
| Find anything | Search box (every lane, every status) | — |
| Pick a project up | Open card → **Start** | `portfolio.py set-status X active` |
| Put one down | Open card → **Park** | `portfolio.py set-status X paused` |
| Finish one | Open card → **Done** | `portfolio.py set-status X done` |
| Say who it's for | Open card → receiver field | `portfolio.py set-receiver X "Kenny Boyd"` |
| Re-prioritise | Drag within a column | — |
| Move a stage | Drag to another column | `portfolio.py set-stage X building` |
| Log a note | Open card → add update, Enter | `portfolio.py add-update X "note"` |
| Capture an idea | — | `portfolio.py add-idea "pitch"` or "new idea: …" to Claude |

**End.** Run `closeout`. It checks the card of every project you touched today, fixes the
gaps with you (below), commits board edits as `data: board edits <date>`, pushes, and
prints the cards last. Those printed cards are what the other machine, or you next month,
picks up from.

**Friday.** `weekly-review` now has a sweep: up to 10 paused projects that nobody has
touched for 30+ days, oldest first. For each you say **revive** (needs a next step and a
receiver), **keep** (parked; it leaves the sweep for 90 days) or **archive**. Anything you
skip comes back next week. 85 are waiting as of 2026-10-03, so about 8 Fridays clears it.

## Reading a card

```
 2  NCAA_BestPractices_Doc                    ← rank in the lane · name
    NCAA best practices document (Chris…)     ← what it is (registry purpose)
    for      Chris Ruf                        ← receiver
    stands   08-04 Confirmed as a separate…   ← newest dated line in STATUS (or registry)
    next     Collect source material and…     ← first item under STATUS ## Next
    touched  yesterday                        ← last file change, either machine
    ▪▪▫▫▫▫ idea 1/6               [paused]    ← stage · status
    7-day rule: 5 days left · needs step 1 done
    ⚠ Needs a receiver
```

- **"nothing on record"** on `stands` or `next` means the STATUS file is thin. That's the
  most common reason a card reads badly, and the fix is in the repo, not the board.
- **"touched"** comes from the landed ledger (30 days). Older means "not in the last month".
- **Flags** are the only red on the page. They mean an active project is missing a next
  step or a receiver.
- **Hover** the `next` line to see whether it came from STATUS or from the registry, and
  the `touched` line for the exact time and machine.

## What makes cards good (the part that's on you)

The board is only as good as STATUS.md. Two habits do almost all of it:

1. **A dated line for each session's progress**, under `## Done` or `## Current state`:
   ```
   - 2026-10-03: Week 5 EPA profile built; ASU game-day sheet sent to coaches.
   ```
   The card shows the newest one. A registry note dated today does *not* count for
   closeout; STATUS is the record.
2. **One concrete first item under `## Next`.** A command to run or a file to open, not a
   theme. "Run `pff_game_result.py --week 6` after PFF grades post" beats "keep going on
   matchups". Strike an item through (`~~done~~`) and the card skips to the next one.

## The rules that push back (on purpose)

- **Slate cap: 5 active job projects.** Start a sixth and the board refuses and says
  which five are active. Park one first. Other lanes are not capped.
- **7-day rule.** Starting a job, side or tool project starts a clock. Within 7 days it
  needs a receiver *and* step 1 done, or the next sync pauses it. The card counts down.
  Re-start it when there's something to show; the clock restarts.
- **Receivers.** Job, side and tool projects name who the output is for: a person, or
  `me: <why>` (a bare "me" is refused). system and knowledge projects are exempt.
- **Focus view hides things.** It shows active projects, paused ones touched in the last
  14 days, and anything with a charter date in the next 14 days. Each column says how many
  it hides. Click **Focus** to switch to **All rows**; the choice is remembered.

## Two machines

The registry travels by git. dev-sync pulls before the board starts; closeout commits and
pushes board edits. The header says **"N unpushed registry edits"** while there are any.
If you edit on Windows and skip closeout, then edit on the Mac, expect a JSON merge
conflict: run closeout before switching machines.

## When something's off

- **`pm` says the board did not start:** the log path is in the message. Usually a bad
  `portfolio.json` (it refuses to start on one; `portfolio.py slate-check` shows the error).
- **A change in the terminal didn't show up:** is the project in the current view (Focus,
  lane tab, search)? Polling only watches the STATUS files of cards on screen.
- **The unpushed-edits count is stale after a push:** it updates on the next registry
  change. Harmless.
- **Undo says "registry changed outside the board":** something else wrote the file since
  your last board edit. Undo refuses rather than wipe that change.

## Your first 30 minutes

Do these with real projects; each one teaches one part.

1. **Open it.** New PowerShell → `pm`. (After a Claude Code restart, `/pm` works too.)
2. **Focus vs All.** Note the job lane's card count, click **Focus** → **All rows**, look at
   the difference, switch back.
3. **Search.** Type `cfb` — the lane tabs show where the hits are.
4. **Fix a real gap.** Weekly_Matchups_2026 is active with "⚠ Needs a receiver". Open it,
   type a receiver (`me: in-season scouting I run`, or a coach's name), click away. The
   flag disappears.
5. **Watch it live.** In the terminal, add a dated line to
   `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Matchups_2026/docs/STATUS.md` (or any visible project's), save,
   and watch its `stands` line change within a few seconds.
6. **Feel the cap.** Start a paused job project. (5 slots, 1 used, so it works.) Then Park
   it again.
7. **Preview tonight.** `python portfolio.py card-check` — the list closeout will walk you
   through: today's touched projects and their gaps.
8. **Preview Friday.** `python portfolio.py sweep` — the first 10 paused projects up for a
   decision. Look before Friday; you may already know the answers.

## Where to look next

- `README.md` — full CLI list and what the board can change.
- `docs/project-management-system-design.md` — why each rule exists, and what was rejected.
- `COMMANDS.md` (DEV root) — the desk reference across all projects.

content.text:
The board now opens at the same address every time, so it can be a Mac app. Tonight on the Mac: `git pull` in project-triage, type `pm`, then in Safari choose File → Add to Dock. I couldn't try that step from Windows, so the Dock app itself is untested.

The fixed address on Windows is http://127.0.0.1:7474/?token=I4t3GhQQNCLhWDOQ_OVuGw, and it held after two restarts. On Windows, Edge's Apps → "Install this site as an app" should do the same thing; I haven't tried that either.

- **Port:** it now defaults to 7474. If something else holds that port, the board uses a free one and tells you, and the Dock app won't find it that time.
- **Token:** it's made once per machine and stored outside DEV, so Google Drive never syncs it. On the Mac it's in `~/.config/pm-board/token`, on Windows in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pm-board\token`. Deleting the file creates a new one, and you'd re-add the Dock app.
- **Windows bug fixed along the way:** a second board could quietly share a port that was already in use, so the board would never have noticed 7474 was taken.
- **Tests:** 3 new ones pass. The full suite has 7 failures, the same 7 as before my change; they come from how subprocesses start in this session and pass when run alone.
- **Docs:** README and GUIDE have a new "As a Mac app" section, and STATUS lists the Mac step for tonight. Pushed as `8b7a699`.
- **The Dock app still needs the board running.** Typing `pm` once a day is enough. On your phone, use Claude with the repo, as we discussed.

I also committed and pushed the board edits you made this afternoon (`data: board edits 2026-10-04`) so the Mac sees them tonight. That was 2:36–2:47 PM: ranks, a receiver, one project marked done, and the Substack side project started.

- **Weekly_Matchups_2026** is active with no charter.

# Plan: Performance Technology Best Practices (NCAA SSI)

Draft 2026-10-04, for agreement with Chris Ruf by **2026-10-14** (charter step 1).
Source material and the full gap analysis: `docs/SOURCES.md`.

## What this document is

A Baylor best-practices document that puts the NCAA SSI *Performance Technologies
Recommendations: Responsible Use in Collegiate Athletics* (CSMAS/SSI, March 2026) into
practice in four areas Chris signs off on:

1. Technology adoption plan
2. Athlete consent
3. Vendor data contracts
4. Staff-transition continuity

**Done means:** Chris signs it off, and it is in use by 2026-12-16.

## Three decisions to get from Chris first

Everything below assumes the recommendation in each. If he picks the other option,
the outline changes, but the schedule doesn't.

| # | Decision | Recommendation | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Best-practice guide or formal department policy? | **Guide plus procedures and forms**, with a one-page policy statement only if Chris wants one | At the 2026-07-30 meeting, leadership preferred "flexible best-practice documents over rigid formal policy". UT chose formal policy (SMED-8055); we can follow its structure without its formality. |
| 2 | How does this relate to the Software & Technology Management Framework (draft, 08-14)? | **This document is the framework's "Version 1" content.** The framework keeps the request and review process (SSI Rec 4). This document supplies what the framework marks "planned for Version 1": the working group, consent, education, the transfer protocol, the feedback loop | Avoids two documents covering the same process. The framework's request process is already built. |
| 3 | Scope: only the four areas, or the four plus education? | **Four areas plus a short education section** | SSI calls education "foundational for informed consent" (Rec 2), so consent can't stand without it. Keep education to who, how often and what topics, not a curriculum. |

## Proposed outline of the document

0. **Purpose and scope.** SSI basis, definitions (SSI's own, as UT does), who it applies to.
1. **Governance.** A standing Performance Technology Working Group: multidisciplinary, with student-athlete members (SSI Rec 1.1). Annual review of this document. Named owner. Medical authority over return-to-play stays with Athletic Medicine (Rec 3.3).
2. **Technology adoption.** Points to the framework's request and review process (Rec 4). Adds only what it lacks: the "start from the question" rule (Iowa State's intake form), and one scoring instrument. Today the March checklist and the framework scorecard compete; reconcile them into one.
3. **Athlete consent and education.**
   - Notice versus consent: which data needs opt-in consent, and which is unavoidable but disclosed. Webinar line: venue tracking is unavoidable, a wearable needs consent.
   - Consent form, built from the March template: voluntary, withdraw without penalty, retention, transfer.
   - Disclosure when de-identified data goes to vendor norm-building.
   - Annual re-consent, and re-consent when a new technology is introduced.
   - Where consent records live.
   - Annual education by group (Rec 2.1–2.3).
4. **Data management.**
   - Ownership, storage, access, and who may interpret and communicate data (Rec 3, 3.1).
   - The physiologic versus performance data classification.
   - Collect only what is used ("if you're not doing anything with it, don't collect it").
   - Transfer-athlete protocol (Rec 3.2).
5. **Vendor data contracts.**
   - A standard data addendum or clause checklist: ownership, permitted use, storage and jurisdiction, AI training, downstream sharing, data-for-discount or norm-pooling terms, retention and deletion, portability, breach notification.
   - **An exit clause:** return or delete data when a product is dropped. Nothing does this today.
   - An audit of existing contracts (about 50 vendors), run with Legal and Procurement.
6. **Staff-transition continuity** (no SSI or framework source; original work).
   - Every platform has a named institutional admin account, never a personal one.
   - Access removal on departure, with a checklist and a timeline.
   - A data custodian per platform, with a backup.
   - A handover note for each system the person ran.
   - Vendor contact and renewal dates recorded in the tech inventory.
7. **Continuous improvement.** An annual student-athlete feedback survey (Rec 5.2), staff feedback (5.3), and a working-group review that revises this document (5.1).
- **Appendices (forms):** consent form, vendor data addendum checklist, offboarding checklist, annual review checklist.

Target length: the guide in about 8–10 pages, with forms separate. Format: Baylor_Doc_Style (docx + pdf).

## Schedule (charter dates in bold)

| When | Step | Output |
|---|---|---|
| By **10/14** | Meet Chris, settle decisions 1–3 and agree this plan | Charter step 1 done |
| 10/15–10/24 | Inputs: Legal/OGC (ownership, HIPAA/FERPA/Texas classification, consent model), Procurement (contract list, addendum), ITS (offboarding, admin accounts), Athletic Medicine (medical authority, physiologic data). Follow up the May outside-counsel proposal | Answers to the open questions; contract list |
| 10/20–11/05 | Draft sections 0–7, reusing the March drafts and the framework text | Draft v1 |
| By **11/06** | First draft to Chris | Charter step 2 |
| 11/09–11/20 | Revise; review the consent form with OGC; review the offboarding checklist with ITS | Draft v2 |
| By **11/25** | Final delivered | Charter step 3 |
| By **12/16** | In use: working group chartered or meeting scheduled; consent form live for spring; Chris confirms | Charter step 4 |

## Who needs to be involved

- **Chris Ruf:** receiver and sign-off.
- **Athletic Medicine:** medical authority, physiologic data.
- **OGC/Legal:** ownership, consent, contracts.
- **Procurement / Business Office:** vendor contracts.
- **ITS:** storage, security, offboarding.
- **Compliance:** education sessions, NIL.
- **Student-athlete voice:** SAAC or similar, for the working group and feedback.

## Risks

- **Legal answers arrive late.** Draft with the March positions marked "pending OGC", so legal review slots in without blocking the draft.
- **The framework draft is parked** (archived repo, "Draft for discussion"). If Chris won't treat it as live, section 2 has to carry the adoption process itself, which means more writing in that section.
- **Contract audit scale** (about 50 vendors). Plan the audit process and a priority list (wearables and force plates first), not the full audit, inside this deadline.

## Questions for the Chris meeting (short list)

1. Decisions 1–3 above.
2. Who owns the document and signs it (UT uses its Chief Medical Officer)?
3. Data ownership position: institution-owned with athlete access (the March draft), or athlete-owned for physiologic data (the framework spec's posture)?
4. Who can we go to in OGC, Procurement and ITS, and did the May outside-counsel proposal go anywhere?
5. Does a working group with student-athlete members get chartered, and can education ride on existing compliance and orientation sessions?

The full open-question list is in `docs/SOURCES.md` § F.

# Sources and gap analysis

Compiled 2026-10-04 by a research pass over the SSI material, the 9/9 webinar, Eric's
March drafts, the Software & Technology framework, and UT's policies. Read-only; no
source was changed. Main finding: the Software & Technology framework fully carries only
SSI Rec 4. The registry note overstated the rest, and **no source addresses
staff-transition continuity** (see D).

Drive folder below = `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\01_PROJECTS\_STALLED\2026-03-05_SSI_PerformanceTechRecs\`
Framework = `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/` (archive hold until 2026-11-02; repo on GitHub, archived)

## A. Source inventory

| Source | What it is | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTechRecommendations.pdf` | NCAA CSMAS/SSI, "Performance Technologies Recommendations: Responsible Use in Collegiate Athletics", 5 pp, March 2026, from the May 2025 Summit | Read in full |
| Drive `SSI_Notes_09092026.docx` | Fireflies-style notes on the 9/9 webinar, organised by theme | Read |
| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-09-09_NCAA_SSI_Webinar__Performance_Tech__Data_Governance.md` | Summary and action items only | Read |
| Fireflies transcript `01M23EEHZ3CRE03AYYADWA3N0D` | Full 45-min SSI Spotlight webinar | Read in full. A keyword search returned 0 results, but a date-range listing found it. |
| Drive `NCAA_Performance_Tech_Action_Plan_DETAILED.docx` | March 2026, roughly 7.5k words: Baylor roadmap per recommendation, with templates (charter, consent form, access matrix, checklist, surveys) | Read |
| Drive `NCAA_SSI_Summary_and_Recommendations.docx` | Memo dated 7 Mar 2026 with a 4-phase plan (Mar → Fall 2026) | Read (some sentences truncated in the source) |
| Drive `NCAA_PerformanceTech_Condensed_v2.docx` | 1-page table: each recommendation, then a Baylor action | Read (text garbled in places) |
| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTech_StaffOverview_v3.md` | Marp staff deck, April 2026 | Read |
| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-05-26_Athlete_Data_Legal_Discussion.md` | Summary of an outside-counsel discussion (proposal for phased policy, vendor-risk, SOP and training work) | Summary only. No transcript found. |
| Framework `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-…design.md` | Design document | Read |
| Framework `deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-14.docx` and `Software_and_Tech_Management_ER_2026-08-14.docx` | 2-page summary and full draft | Read |
| Framework `docs/TALKING_POINTS_ER_2026-08-13_internal.md` | Internal talking points | Read |
| Framework `UT_Technology Policies and Procedures/` SMED-8055 policy, PROC-SMED-8055, SMED-8110 | Peer examples | Read |
| UT `Human Performance Release.pdf` | Scanned image. A 2015-dated **assumption-of-risk / liability waiver**, **not** a data-consent form. | Viewed |

UT's policy lists a "Student-Athlete Informed Consent Form – Performance Technology Use",
but that form is not in the folder.

## B. SSI recommendations (PDF structure)

The PDF uses three kinds of statement (p1, Fig. 1): **Foundational**, **Recommendation**
and **Strategy**.

**Foundational statements (p2)**
- **Fundamentals.**
  - Performance technology is defined broadly: "devices that enable users to collect and record biometric and/or performance data", including "cameras, sensors, surveys, software, mobile apps".
  - It is "just one tool".
  - Quality varies (accuracy, reliability, validity, function) and should be assessed "prior to selecting or implementing".
- **Rights and Protections.**
  - Schools need to understand "student-athlete rights and protections" and "applicable local and international laws".
  - Unintended impacts "including implications for mental health" matter.
- **Written Plan.** Covers how groups are educated, how data is managed, how purchase and implementation decisions are made, and how continuous improvement works.

**Rec 1 – Policy (p3).** Establish a written plan.
- 1.1: a multidisciplinary team develops, "routinely" reviews and revises it (student-athletes, sports medicine, coaches, athletics administration, legal affairs, IT).
